name: Smart lamp
tagline: Voice & motion-activated ambient smart lamp with OLED dashboard
summary: Wisp continuously measures VOCs, CO2 concentration, ambient temperature, and relative humidity. An animated OLED dashboard visualizes indoor air comfort indexes and triggers an acoustic alarm whenever volatile gas spikes are detected.

parts.name: ESP32 DevKit V1
parts.why: Dual-core 240MHz MCU with 12-bit ADC channels and onboard 2.4GHz WiFi/BLE.

parts.name: MQ-135 Air Quality & Hazardous Gas Sensor
parts.why: Sensitive SnO2 electro-chemical sensor for NH3, NOx, alcohol, benzene, and smoke.

parts.name: DHT11 Temperature & Relative Humidity Sensor
parts.why: Digital calibrated ambient temperature (0-50°C) and humidity (20-90% RH) probe.

parts.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display
parts.why: High-contrast monochrome display showing live ppm graphs and comfort status.

parts.name: 5V Active Piezo Buzzer
parts.why: Audible alert sounder for hazardous indoor air conditions.

product.pageHeadline: Breathe cleaner air in your home and creative studio.
bullets: Precision MQ-135 sensor detecting carbon monoxide, ammonia, benzene, and smoke
Microsecond temperature and relative humidity tracking for optimal comfort
Translucent frosted enclosure with directional ambient airflow channels
Dual-core ESP32 architecture capable of local MQTT and Home Assistant telemetry

buildSteps: Step 1: 3D print the vented Wisp case and snap-fit lid using frosted acrylic or clear resin.
Step 2: Press-fit the ESP32 DevKit into the base retaining clips.
Step 3: Insert the MQ-135 gas sensor facing the side ventilation honeycomb.
Step 4: Mount the DHT11 temp/humidity probe and connect data line to GPIO4.
Step 5: Install the OLED display into the lid bezel window and wire I2C SDA/SCL to GPIO21/22.
Step 6: Connect the piezo buzzer to GPIO18 and power on via USB Type-C.
